small_guidance:
- Add larger tile configs targeting M=1024, N=8192, K=8192: try BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 with num_warps=8/num_stages=4, and BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=32 with num_warps=8/num_stages=5 to better overlap K-loads given large K=8192.
- Drop the masked-K tail path by asserting K%BLOCK_K==0 (true here for K=8192) and use unmasked `tl.load` in the K-loop, reducing per-iter mask overhead. Also use `tl.multiple_of` / `tl.max_contiguous` hints on `offs_am`/`offs_bn` to enable wider vector loads.
- Cache `wT` once in `__init__` (move outside forward) and skip the `x.cuda()` call when already on GPU; eliminates per-call cache check overhead.
large_guidance:
- Consider a split-K or stream-K GEMM: with M=1024, N=8192 the grid has only 64 row-tiles × 64 col-tiles = 4096 programs at 128×128 (fine), but K=8192 dominates — a split-K (e.g. SPLIT_K=2-4) with atomic-add epilogue could improve SM utilization, then run the activation epilogue in a second tiny kernel only on the final accumulator.
- Switch weight storage to pre-transposed `[K, N]` contiguous at init time so the hot inner loads of B are stride-1 along N (already done), but also pre-fuse `bias + add_value` into a single vector at init/forward-prologue (since both broadcast along M identically) — saves one global load per N-tile.
- Explore TF32 `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` (default on Ampere) and ensure inputs are cast appropriately; on RTX 4090 (Ada), tensor cores hit peak with FP16/BF16 — consider an FP16 matmul path with FP32 accumulator if numerics allow under the 5e-2 tolerance.
